articles.title: Most coding agent benchmarks skip large-scale refactoring. Not this one.
articles.text:
Most coding agent benchmarks skip large-scale refactoring. Not this one.
AI coding agents still struggle with large-scale refactoring, with the best model achieving only a 41.2% resolve rate on a new refactoring-focused benchmark developed byresearchers at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Peking University, Douyin Group, and other institutions.
It’s no secret that AI benchmarks aren’t perfect. A recent audit cited by the researchers shows how misleading AI coding agent benchmarks can be, with nearly 60% of unsolved SWE-bench Verified instances containing flawed tests.
“We don’t have LLMs that would be able to read a large codebase and see it in its entirety and ‘understand’ it all at once,” he says. “That level of capability is still far out of reach.”
For AI coding agents, specifically, evaluation quality is considered to be on the decline, as frontier models can end up sailing through benchmarks if solutions have leaked into training sets. But when models can manage impressive-looking scores without really doing all the work, it raises the question of whether those benchmarks are truly a good indication of real-world agent capabilities.
As Vojtěch Pavlík, senior director of technical strategy, core infrastructure, SUSE, tells The New Stack, many sought-after capabilities are still a ways away:
“We don’t have LLMs that would be able to read a large codebase and see it in its entirety and ‘understand’ it all at once,” he says. “That level of capability is still far out of reach.”
A new benchmark attempts to clear things up. SWE-Bench ProMax is a multilingual code refactoring benchmark of 170 instances from real commits across seven programming languages (Python, Java, TypeScript, Go, C, C++, and Rust). Per its creators, every instance underwent multi-stage curation to address the quality problems found in other benchmarks: They wrote issue descriptions to make them more precise; manually reviewed test suites to remove overly narrow or broad tests; and filtered out tasks with insufficient complexity or limited cross-file scope.
The result is a benchmark that frontier models struggle to solve.
Why large-scale refactoring stumps coding agents
By focusing SWE-Bench ProMax on large-scale refactoring, researchers say the new benchmark “presents a meaningful and unsaturated challenge for current AI coding agents.”
That’s because refactoring is hard. “Strict refactoring demands zero tolerance for error, zero tolerance for behavior changes, and complete reversibility,” Shane Warden, principal architect, ActiveState, tells The New Stack. For him, the question of whether or not current AI tools can successfully handle large-scale refactoring depends on whether source code is considered plain prose or a deterministic, structured graph of information:
“I don’t believe that premise. I believe that token proximity does not guarantee structural understanding.”
“Engineers who view LLMs primarily as text-processing engines treat refactoring as a text-generation task,” he says, explaining that developers who take this approach feed an entire codebase into a large context window, prompt the model, and then wait for a series of multi-file diffs.
But he’s not buying that take. “This approach relies on the premise that current LLMs express a deep understanding of large systems,” continues Warden. “I don’t believe that premise. I believe that token proximity does not guarantee structural understanding.”
Pavlík adds another problem, saying that attention — or a lack thereof — also complicates large-scale refactoring:
“For very large LLMs, a highly optimized attention algorithm, like DSA [Deepseek Sparse Attention] and similar others are basically a requirement to get any usable performance,” he says. “For changes in a large, complex, or convoluted codebase that maxes out the context window, this can easily result in missing important observations and generally getting confused.”
Beyond context and attention woes, Pavlík calls out time as a fundamental factor in software that further trips up LLMs, pointing to race condition errors, loss of idempotency, loss of atomicity, and incorrect retry handling as problems that emerge when parallel tasks execute in different orders, i.e., what he says happens “where code meets time.”
“People live in a world based on time,” he says. “LLMs, not so much. You get code that passes all tests and works on a sunny day if the user does the tasks exactly as described in the contract/manifest/spec, but fails miserably when a user clicks a button twice in a quick succession, when a connection times out on a network, or when two tasks finish at nearly the same time, overwriting each others results.”
With all these factors at play, it’s easy to see why many benchmarks overlook large-scale refactoring — but that’s precisely why they need it. Without tests on complex, cross-file work, how can developers judge what agents can really do?
What SWE-Bench ProMax tests that most benchmarks miss
Most coding agent benchmarks are designed to run quickly and produce reasonably deterministic, verifiable solutions. “This rules out large-scale refactoring tasks,” Pavlík tells The New Stack.
He also says it’s why most LLM benchmarks today are compromised, as they often exercise models on only small contexts where they’re at their best. Plus, “many current frontier LLMs know the answers to most common benchmarks by heart by now,” Pavlík adds. “The more ubiquitous a benchmark becomes, the less reliable the results are.”
With this new refactoring-focused benchmark, Pavlík sees it as a sign that tests are becoming more complex and less learnable upfront so they can better expose where agents struggle:
“SWE-Bench ProMax is an example of how benchmarks are moving, from the ‘we need to measure how good the LLM is’ approach to ‘we need LLMs to improve on a particular task’ approach.”
What will it take to make agents better at refactoring?
Building a benchmark that can identify holes in agent performance is one thing. But what will it take to plug them up?
For his part, Pavlík calls for a multi-layered approach, where developers first analyze and map the codebase to create detailed specifications, use retrieval-augmented generation to recall relevant parts of the code, rather than leaning purely on attention, and bring humans in for validation. He also advises implementing a fully detailed test suite for the original codebase to make sure it’s correct before starting refactoring.
Warden puts forth a similar idea: “To me, the most promising research focuses on LLMs driving deterministic, structurally aware developer tooling instead of LLMs writing out raw multi-file diffs.”
He describes an architecture where the LLM recognizes code smells, evaluates design trade-offs, and queries Language Server Protocols (LSPs) and code graph tooling to analyze explicit code structures, dependencies, and data flows, issuing small, zero-entropy commands to execute changes and rolling back those changes if tests fail.
Benchmarks are never going to provide a perfect measure of real-world performance, but leaving out difficult tasks like refactoring paints an overly rosy picture of agent capabilities. SWE-Bench ProMax may just bring in some realism.

articles.title: GIGABYTE Intros B550 X Gaming Socket AM4 Motherboard
articles.text:
Thursday, August 20th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
GIGABYTE Intros B550 X Gaming Socket AM4 Motherboard
Supporting the recent Socket AM4 renaissance sparked by the memory pricing crisis is a new crop of motherboards, and GIGABYTE's latest addition is the B550 X Gaming. The board brings many of GIGABYTE's recent motherboard innovations to the aged platform. It is build in the ATX form-factor, and draws power from a combination of 24-pin ATX and 8-pin EPS connectors, conditioning it for the processor with an 8+2 phase duet-rail VRM that's sufficient to power the Ryzen 7 5800X3D. The socket is wired to four DDR4 DIMM slots, a PCI-Express 4.0 x16 slot, and an M.2 Gen 4 x4 NVMe slot. The board's second M.2 slot is Gen 3 x4, and wired to the B550 FCH, along with four SATA 6 Gbps ports. Other expansion slots include a PCI-Express x16 (electrical Gen 3 x4), and two PCIe x1.
The board features M.2 EZ-Latch design that makes it easy to install the M.2 SSD and the included heatsink for the M.2 Gen 4 NVMe slot. The board also features newer ARGB 2.0 headers. Display connectivity includes one each of standard DisplayPort and HDMI 2.1. There is no WLAN connectivity, the board's sole network connectivity is a 2.5 GbE interface driven by a Realtek 8125-series PHY. The board's onboard audio solution features an entry-level Realtek ALC892 codec. USB connectivity includes one 10 Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 2 port, three 5 Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports, one 5 Gbps USB type-C, two USB 2.0 ports on the rear panel, with two additional USB 3.2 ports via headers, and multiple USB 2.0 headers. Expect a price well under $150.

7 Comments on GIGABYTE Intros B550 X Gaming Socket AM4 Motherboard
There's no way that this can be considered a value or budget option when anything attached to this is grossly overpriced.
About AM4, the 3rd world exists so there's market for it. Not everyone needs the latest, and with the current RAM prices not everyone can afford it. Yes, LGA1700 is a great alternative with better IO, but that doesn't make AM4 outright bad.
AMD make a lower nm version of zen 3 and maybe some higher clock speeds. Since they keep releasing new cpu on old technology.
Im not complaining. Im still happy with my 5600X and 5950X cpu's.
Best we can have is the 5800x3d anniversary - which is already an excellent bone AMD threw us! The node is so mature and the 3D cache also getting there who knows, maybe they'll do a higher clock 5850X3D about 5% faster than the original to offer the ultimate stopgap :D
The storage system is rarely local console and often had a past life as a gaming desktop or unretired eWaste converted to low power storage duty.
Accessibility is the real question in these situations. The data can sit across multiple HDDs if it's large volume or multiple SSDs if it needs to be fast.
Those of us that figured it out realize M.2 and sata are precious, so every volume connected to them is data. The OS doesn't need more than USB2.
For those of us dabbling in RAID volumes, it makes sense to have similar access speeds on sata and M.2 or we start looking into volume adapters.
This would be an okay board if we're able to attach several x1 and x4 cards to it but any of us that have experienced B550/X570 know we can't fill it.
This board is a joke at any price.

articles.title: Parabelflug, Stratosphärenballon, Weltraumreisen: Dieser Mann lockt mit überirdischen Tripps
articles.text:
Keine „Raketenwissenschaft“: Wie dieser Mann die passende Weltraumreise für Reiche arrangiert
Dieser Mann verwirklicht schon seit Langem die kühnsten Reiseträume: In über zwei Jahrzehnten als Mitinhaber des Luxus-Lifestyle-Unternehmens „Roman & Erica“ hat Roman Chiporukha fast alles organisiert. Von der Betreuung des Baus der Superyacht eines Kunden bis zu Urlauben auf den Bahamas an einem Ort, der so abgeschieden ist, dass Gäste eine Verschwiegenheitserklärung unterzeichnen müssen, war alles dabei.
Diese Erfahrungen haben ihm, wie er sagt, das Vertrauen einer „ultra-vermögenden Zielgruppe“ eingebracht. Dies führte dann auch zu einem für ihn lebensverändernden Telefonanruf: Im Jahr 2018 suchte Axiom Space nach sogenannten Citizen Explorers mit tiefen Taschen, die bereit waren, jeweils 50 Millionen US-Dollar zu investieren, um an der ersten gänzlich privaten Mission zur Internationalen Raumstation ISS teilzunehmen – im April 2022.
Keine „Raketenwissenschaft“: Wie suborbitale Flüge schmackhaft gemacht werden sollen
Der Vorgang zeigte Chiporukha, dass nicht der Himmel nicht mehr die Grenze seiner Arbeit war, sondern die Marktnachfrage. Er gewann erfolgreich einen privaten ISS-Astronauten als Kunden und gründete dann 2021 die Firma SpaceVIP. Dort will er Weltraumerlebnisse anbieten, die Kultur, Wissenschaft und Nutzen für die Menschheit miteinander verbinden. Der Job ist speziell und hat sehr spezifische Anforderungen.
Chiporukha ist selbst weder Astronaut noch Luft- und Raumfahrtingenieur, daher musste er sich in kürzester Zeit mit den Feinheiten der kommerziellen Raumfahrt vertraut machen. Um bei Privatpersonen keine allzu großen Kopfschmerzen zu der bildlichen und wörtlichen „Raketenwissenschaft“ hervorzurufen, hat er den stark fragmentierten Raumfahrtsektor in ein einziges digitales Portal gebündelt. Dort können Kund:innen nun suborbitale Flüge und andere ausgefallene Reiserouten genauso mühelos recherchieren wie einen Wochenendausflug mit Weltraummotiv.
Das Portal reicht aber nicht: Er betont gegenüber den Kund:innen, dass sie trotz der digitalen Hilfe weiterhin einen erfahrenen Vermittler benötigen, der „alle notwendige Vergünstigungen, eine individuelle Wunscherfüllung sowie Upgrades“ besorgen kann.
Zusammenarbeit mit Axiom, Blue Origin, SpaceX und Virgin Galactic
SpaceVIP erhält jeden Monat Dutzende Anfragen, doch Chiporukha unterstützt nur einen kleinen, exklusiven Kund:innenkreis dabei, maßgeschneiderte Reisen zu entwerfen, die auf dem jeweiligen Budget sowie der körperlichen Komfortzone basieren. Als Brücke zwischen den reichen Weltraumträumern und den strengen luft- und raumfahrttechnischen Vorgaben arbeitet er mit Anbietern wie Axiom für mehrtägige Aufenthalte auf der ISS sowie mit Blue Origin, SpaceX und Virgin Galactic für andere Arten von Raumausflügen zusammen.
Interessierte können sich beispielsweise als Einstieg für einen Parabelflug in der Schwerelosigkeit oder eine sanfte sechsstündige Reise an Bord eines Stratosphärenballons in rund 24 Kilometern Höhe über der Erde entscheiden. Das seien „relativ erschwingliche“ Abenteuer, wenn man zu den Menschen gehört, für die ein paar hunderttausend US-Dollar nicht allzu viel sind.
Digitalförster
Manager für Weltraumschrott
Hitzemanager
Wettermacher
CO₂-Buchhalter
Spezialist für Klimagerechtigkeit
Wer züchtet die Pilze für den medizinischen Markt?
Was muss ein biologischer Risikoberater können?
Forscherin sucht störende Lichtquellen im All
Eine neue Generation inspirieren
Das Geschäft mit den Weltraumreisen bleibt in Bezug auf Kosten und Technik ein mühsamer Weg. Aber, betont Chiporukha, es müssten einfach mehr Menschen ein Interesse daran entwickeln. Er ist selbst Mitbegründer der Space Prize Foundation, einer gemeinnützigen Organisation, die Wissenschaftswettbewerbe für junge Frauen und in MINT-Fächern unterrepräsentierte Gruppen veranstaltet.
Die Gewinner:innen erhalten Zugriff auf Parabelflüge und eine Teilnahme an Astronauten-Ausbildungsprogrammen auf der Erde. „Um Raumfahrt mehr zum Mainstream zu machen, reicht es nicht aus, nur die Kosten für das Ticket zu senken“, sagt der Weltraumreiseleiter. „Es geht darum, Zugang zu dieser Branche zu schaffen und den Menschen zu vermitteln, dass diese in Zukunft nicht nur einer winzigen Gruppe vorbehalten sein wird.“
Was Astronauten mit ins Weltall nehmen

articles.title: Bambu Lab P1S Combo 3D printer is under $500 everywhere I look
articles.text:
The excellent Bambu Lab P1S Combo brings multicolor 3D printing to your desk, and it's $50 off right now
It works out of the box, and you'll be ready to print in 15 minutes
The Bambu Lab P1S Combo is designed to remove much of the tinkering traditionally associated with 3D printing. It arrives assembled, can be set up in around 15 minutes, and automatically handles jobs such as bed leveling and vibration compensation before you start printing.
Currently, the Bambu Lab P1S Combo 3D printer is down to $499 (was $549) at Bambu Lab with free shipping. I've also seen it on sale for $500 at Amazon, and at Best Buy right now. So, you're saving almost a dollar going direct, but there are plenty of options here.
Alongside common materials such as PLA and PETG, the P1S supports ABS, and its combination of high acceleration and automatic calibration is designed to deliver fast prints without any loss of quality.
The P1S uses 1.75mm filament and comes fitted with a 0.4mm nozzle. It supports PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA and ABS, while Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a microSD slot provide connectivity and local storage options.
- Also on sale for $499.99 at Best Buy and at Amazon
Why we recommend it
Ease of use is one of the P1S Combo's biggest benefits. It arrives assembled, requires relatively little initial setup and handles important calibration tasks automatically.
The AMS gives the Combo considerably more creative potential than the printer alone. Automatic filament switching opens the door to multicolor models without requiring you to manually swap spools throughout a print.
Its enclosed body is useful if you want to move beyond basic PLA projects. Combined with its speed, automatic calibration and broad material compatibility, the P1S is a machine you aren't likely to outgrow quickly.
For more options, check out our roundup of the best 3D printers you can buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Bambu Lab P1S Combo if...
You want to get into more ambitious 3D printing without spending your time manually configuring the printer before every job. Automatic bed leveling and vibration compensation take care of some of the routine setup, making the P1S a good choice if you want to concentrate on what you're making rather than constantly adjusting the machine.
The Combo is also the one to choose for easy multicolor printing.
❌ Skip the Bambu Lab P1S Combo if...
You only want to make straightforward single-color PLA prints. In that case, you're paying extra for an enclosed printer and the AMS when a simpler model will cover your needs for less.
Price context & historical value
This is about as low as the P1S Combo goes on sale currently. You're saving a cent shy of a dollar by going direct to Bambu Lab, but it's a good price at all three retailers.
At Amazon, it's at its at an all-time low, which also dropped to $500 back in July, but usually holds steady at around the $550 mark. And it's price-matched over at Best Buy, too.
It's not the biggest discount for the fully-enclosed 3D printer, but it's a good choice if multicolor printing is on your wishlist.
For more savings, we track the best 3D printer deals with updates every week.
The Catch: What to know before you buy
The AMS is the main reason to choose the Combo, but not every filament is equally suitable for use with it. Flexible materials such as TPU can require different handling, so don't assume every material supported by the P1S can simply be loaded into the AMS.
The P1S also prioritizes printing rather than giving you a sophisticated onboard interface. Its 2.7-inch display is relatively basic, although you'll likely spend considerably more time controlling and monitoring prints through Bambu Lab's software anyway.

articles.title: Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: the new bar for mainstream Windows laptop excellence
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Dell XPS 13 returns as an excellent Windows-based answer to the MacBook Neo. It’s no performance powerhouse, but at just 2.2 pounds, with 8GB and 16GB options and nearly 15 hours of battery life in our testing, it’s an excellent option for students or mainstream users who don’t need more CPU or GPU muscle.
Pros
- +Premium, affordable thin-and-light design
- +Long battery life
- +8GB and 16GB versions available
- +Free of bloat
- +Excellent speakers
Cons
- -Wildcat Lake CPU performance is limited
- -Weak GPU performance
- -8GB model gets laggy fast when multitasking
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
A year after killing off its long-running XPS premium consumer brand, Dell did an about-face at CES early this year, promising new models, including the redesigned XPS 13 we’re looking at here. But between Dell’s announcement and the XPS 13’s launch, Apple stunned the portable PC world with its budget-priced, unquestionably pretty MacBook Neo, at a starting price of $599 (which got bumped up to $699 in June), leaving even Windows die-hards wondering how PC makers were going to compete in the budget and mid-range laptop space.
Dell clearly decided the XPS 13 was its answer to the Neo, giving it a starting price of $699 for the model with 8GB of RAM (comparable to the Neo), or $899 for the 16GB model. Both options sport the same 512GB of SSD storage and an Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 (Wildcat Lake) CPU. We tested both the 8GB and 16GB models, though there is little difference outside of memory capacity.
Design of the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
The XPS 13 may lack the design flourishes of previous XPS models (there is no carbon fiber to be found), but if I had to describe the new XPS 13’s look in one word, it would be “refined.” Available in the silver “sky” color of our review unit, or a darker gray “storm” hue, all the edges are rounded, and the all-aluminum chassis feels premium, with only some slight flex. And I like the understated branding, with a slim, mirrored XPS logo on top and a smaller mirrored Dell logo underneath.
It’s a look that generally doesn’t stray far from the Apple laptop standard, but the XPS 13 actually feels better in the hands than the MacBook Neo. At 11.69 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches, the Dell’s dimensions roughly match the Neo (11.71 x 8.12 x 0.5 inches), but the XPS is a half-pound lighter (2.2 pounds for the Dell versus 2.7 pounds for the Apple), and Dell tapers its edges more, making it feel slimmer. Both are attractive laptops, to be sure, but having held them both side-by-side, I slightly prefer the XPS 13. And considering how much the MacBook Neo wowed the consumer tech world earlier this year, that’s an impressive achievement from Dell.
Port selection is relegated to a single USB-C port on either side. But with the XPS 13, both are 10 Gbps ports that support DisplayPort 2.1 and charging, while Apple’s competition has one 10 Gbps port and one much slower USB 2.0 port (both are USB-C). Apple does include a headphone jack, which the XPS 13 lacks, and that will be annoying for some. But Dell includes a keyboard backlight while Apple leaves your fingers to fumble around in the dark. Personally, I’d take a backlight over an audio jack any day.
The only thing I don’t love about the new XPS 13’s design is the somewhat sharp edge of metal at the bottom rear, behind the exhaust vents. Because the laptop is so slim and light, I found myself grabbing it by any and all angles, and this is the one area where it doesn’t feel premium or comfortable to hold.
Dell XPS 13 (2026) Specifications
| CPU | Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 | 
| Graphics | Intel Graphics (2 Xe cores) | 
| Memory | 8GB or 16GB (single-channel LPDDR5 at 7467 MT/s) | 
| Storage | 512GB SSD | 
| Display | 13.4-inch, 2560 x 1600, touch | 
| Networking | Intel Wi-Fi 7 BE213 2x2, Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Ports | 2x USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps) | 
| Camera | 1080p, IR | 
| Battery | 52 Whr | 
| Power Adapter | 65W USB-C | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Home | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 11.69 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches | 
| Weight | 2.2 pounds (1 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $699 (8GB), $899 (16GB) | 
Productivity Performance on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
We tested both the 8GB and 16GB variants of the XPS 13. Aside from RAM capacity, the two machines share the same Intel “Wildcat Lake” Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU, with two Performance cores that can Turbo up to 4.6 GHz and four Efficient cores that can hit 3.4 GHz.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Both systems also make do with 512GB of SSD storage (there are no other capacity options). As we’ll get into in our testing, while the performance is roughly similar, our XPS systems had two different drives: one from SK hynix and the other from Kioxia.
As for comparisons, we’ve included the similarly priced (at least to the 8GB mode) MacBook Neo. And on the Windows side, we’ve included the Chuwi UniBook, which has a plastic chassis and a lesser Wildcat Lake CPU, as well as Dell’s XPS 14 with a more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 CPU and a much higher price of nearly $2,000 as tested.
On Geekbench 6, the XPS 13 bested the Chuwi UniBook with its lesser Core 3 304 CPU, but fell behind the MacBook Neo, and by no small amount on the single-core test. The pricier, Panther Lake-powered XPS 14, interestingly, fell right in line with XPS 13 on this test. But as we’ll see next, that doesn’t mean the two systems perform the same on all tasks.
With eight cores and a higher power envelope to work with, the XPS 14 easily led here, converting our 4K test file to 1080p in under seven minutes. This points out the benefits of a higher-powered system for doing compute-intensive tasks like video editing. The XPS 13, particularly the 8GB model, was a bit behind the MacBook Neo, while the Chuwi laptop lagged more than a minute behind everything else.
Both versions of the Dell XPS 13 looked good in our 25GB file transfer test, but the 16GB model was significantly faster. Dell, like most laptop makers, doesn’t guarantee drive models in specific laptops. But in our two units, the 16GB model had an SK hynix PVC10 SSD, while the 8GB model sported a Kioxia BG7 (both drives are 512GB).
The SK hynix drive was about 350 MB/s faster here, but the MacBook Neo was about half as fast as even the slower XPS 13, and the Chuwi UniBook was half as fast again, not a whole lot faster than a spinning-platter hard drive.
If you’re wondering about gaming on the XPS 13, you probably shouldn’t, unless you’re a fan of retro titles and 2D side-scrollers. The CPU’s integrated graphics make do with just two Intel Xe cores.
In 3DMark’s Steel Nomad, neither the 8GB XPS 13 nor the Chuwi UniBook (which also has 8GB of RAM) would run the test. The MacBook Neo (369) easily edged past the 16GB XPS 13 (369). But the Panther Lake-powered Dell XPS 14 (with twice as many Xe cores) more than doubled the results of its smaller sibling.
To stress test the CPU in laptops, we run 10 loops of Cinebench 2026. The 16GB version of the system started with a score of 1,443, dipped to 1,374, but then ramped up (presumably as the cooking kicked in) to 1701, and then finished the rest of its runs steadily in the high 1600s. During the test, the laptop’s Core 5 320 CPU’s six cores averaged a clock speed of 3.13 GHz.
Interestingly, the 8GB model of the XPS 13 (which again has the same CPU) scored slightly lower than the 16GB version on all but the second run. And that’s likely down solely to the memory limitation. As the benchmark’s developer Maxson explains, running Cinebench 2026 on a system with less than 8.5 GB of RAM “will utilize virtual memory, which triggers a significant amount of paging, lowering the achievable performance.”
There’s little doubt that demanding real-world applications will cause similar performance dips. So even if you think you’re good about closing tabs or don’t otherwise do a lot of multitasking, you may get better performance out of the 16GB model. And if you regularly do demanding tasks like editing video or any kind of rendering, you should opt for something more powerful. Wildcat Lake laptops and the MacBook Neo are designed for lightweight tasks like Web browsing and basic document creation.
8GB vs 16GB
Outside of benchmarks, the biggest question between the 8GB and 16GB configurations is: What is it actually like to use Windows 11 on these systems?
The short answer, unsurprisingly, is that 16GB is better. With 15 identical tabs open in Chrome, the 16GB system just ran smoother. You might have to look closely at the Windows animations to notice, but they were far more fluid with more memory. And more importantly, switching back and forth between tabs was faster on the 16GB version, with the 8GB systems’ browser often blinking white before showing a page again.
Chrome (as well as multiple other browsers) does offer a feature to put tabs to sleep while you're not using them. If you're a multitasker in the browser, you'll absolutely want to make sure this is turned on.
For even the most basic tasks, it would behoove Microsoft to make Windows as efficient as possible, because it shouldn't take just a few tabs to start making the experience worse.
Displays on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
Dell doesn’t specify the panel type it uses for the XPS 13, but the 2560 x 1600 touch display generally looks good. And its 30-120 Hz refresh is a nice touch that should help battery life in some scenarios. We did, though, notice an issue with our 16GB review unit. When playing back video, the screen often flickered during bright scenes – but only when running on battery. It went away once the laptop was plugged in, which led me to dig into the display settings, where I noticed the dynamic refresh rate was set to be turned off when on battery. Enabling variable refresh made the flickering go away. Dell told us dynamic research should be told on by default.
There is a separate display wrinkle, though. When placing the 8GB and 16GB models side-by-side, there were some clear differences between the two panels. The 8GB’s screen had deeper blacks, but noticeable backlight glow along the edges of the black bars while watching movie trailers. The 16GB model, however, had worse viewing angles. So both screens had their own upsides and drawbacks. Interestingly, as we’ll see below, the two panels' measurements are quite similar, but one is made by Sharp, while the other is from LG.
Like the SSDs, Dell told us that it is multi-sourcing panels. "You’ve seen some variances with individual panels, but each panel should meet the specs set out for XPS 13," a Dell representative told Tom's Hardware.
In our testing, the XPS 13’s screen delivered over 100% of the sRGB gamut, and roughly 75% of the larger DCI-P3 space.
The MacBook Neo’s screen was similarly colorful, but at a measured 452.6 nits, it’s a little brighter than the XPS 13’s panel, which topped out just below 400 nits. But the XPS panels also include touch, which all MacBooks still lack (at least for now). Both the Dell and the Apple systems deliver great screens for machines in this price range. The Chuwi, while a cheaper laptop, also delivers a screen that’s much less colorful and dimmer than the competition.
Keyboard and touchpad on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
I wouldn’t call the XPS 13’s chiclet-style keyboard one of its strong suits – key travel is fairly shallow, and the keys feel a little stiff. But the slight travel isn’t surprising in a laptop that’s half an inch thick, and I feel like I would get used to the slight stiffness fairly quickly. I didn’t notice any layout issues that confused my fingers, and I could see myself happily using this keyboard for hours a day without any real complaints.
The chiclet style differs from what Dell offers on the XPS 14 and XPS 16, which has the keys placed next to each other in a "lattice-free" design. While I wish there was a bit more travel on the XPS 13, I personally prefer the more traditional chiclet keys over what the company is doing with its larger XPS options.
The touchpad is fairly roomy for a laptop this small, at over five inches. And it’s a physical click pad rather than haptic, but it doesn’t feel cheap. It performed well during my testing time, and is otherwise unremarkable. I like that its top is set just slightly recessed below the deck so both my eyes and my fingers always know where it starts and ends, unlike the previous version of the XPS 13, where its haptic pad was built seamlessly into the wrist area.
That said, the XPS 13’s trackpad, as is traditionally the case, only clicks when you press on or near the bottom. The Neo’s trackpad is also mechanical, but lets you click wherever your fingers land. I don’t particularly find the Neo’s trackpad feature a substantial advantage, but if you’re used to a haptic touchpad, being able to click anywhere on the pad might feel more familiar.
Audio on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
One thing I wasn’t expecting from the XPS 13 was great-sounding speakers. But for a system this slim and a price below $1,000, the quad-speaker setup here left my ears pleasantly surprised. I listened to Portion Control’s “Brain Scraper Death Dive (Rebuild),” and the 8W of peak output filled my home office with a surprising level of sound, without noticeable distortion, even at 100% volume. There’s even some noticeable bass – within reason, mind you. This is a half-inch thick, 2.2-pound laptop. But considering the XPS 13’s svelte frame and its starting price, the speakers and tuning are excellent.
Upgradability of the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
There are only four tiny Torx screws to remove on the bottom of the XPS 13. But after doing that, getting into the laptop was still quite difficult. Dell recommends prying with your thumbs from the rear center. That didn’t work for me no matter how hard I pushed. Eventually, with the help of a plastic pick-style pry tool, I was able to release a few clips near the slim side vents, then work my way around the edges. The clips where Dell recommends starting from near the rear center were the last to release, and some of the most tenacious I have dealt with in several years.
Once finally inside, there isn’t much to do except stare into the abyss of the stealth-black interior. Swapping the short 2230 M.2 SSD in the upper-right corner should be pretty easy. And replacing the battery down the road doesn’t look too difficult. But that’s all you’re likely to change in here.
Perhaps most interesting for such a small laptop, Dell has equipped the XPS 13 with a pair of fans. Fan noise was audible as a whir, but I really only noticed it during our lengthy Cinebench 2026 stress test. And honestly, if you’re running tasks that tax the CPU for several minutes at a time like this, you should probably opt for something more powerful anyway.
Battery life on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
The XPS 13 did well compared to similar options in our battery test, which consists of web browsing, running OpenGL tests, and streaming videos with the screen at 150 nits while connected to Wi-Fi. Both the 8GB and 16GB models of the XPS 13 easily topped 14 hours, which is roughly an hour to 90 mins more than the MacBook Neo and slightly better than the Chuwi.
Of particular interest is the half-hour shorter time on the 8GB model. Some of that difference could easily be down to testing variance. But the 8GB version we tested has a Kioxia BG7 SSD, while the 16GB version has an SK Hynix PVC10. Both are DRAMless drives, but the Hynix drive may be more power-efficient during our battery benchmark.
At well over 20 hours, though, it’s the XPS 14 that walks away with the competition here, helped by the fact that its screen is a lower resolution (1,920 x 1,200) than most of the competition here. Still, an extra five-plus hours of unplugged productivity is another reason why you might want to pay more for the slightly larger-screened Dell.
A laptop charger worth calling out
We don’t typically write much about chargers in laptop reviews, but the one that Dell includes with the XPS 13 is exactly the type that I’ve been asking laptop makers to shift to for years now. It’s a tiny charger with folding prongs that’s more typical of the type you might use with a smartphone, and it has a removable cable.
Given that some of the best chargers we’ve tested can charge laptops and are much smaller than a typical laptop brick, it’s nice to finally see a company ship a compact charger with a laptop that is on par in terms of portability with something you can buy yourself for about $25 or less. It would be even nicer if Dell had included a second USB-C port on the power brick so you could charge both your laptop and smartphone at the same time, but I guess I shouldn’t expect miracles. Still, I applaud Dell for including a compact charger with the XPS 13 and hope to see similar chargers from competing PC makers soon.
Heat on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
During our 10-loop Cinebench 2026 stress test, the XPS 13’s keyboard got warm up near the top row, where we measured the temperature at 104 degrees Fahrenheit, but that was above 4 key, not where fingers typically rest. The touchpad (87 F) and keyboard deck (88.5 F) remained cooler, though. The bottom of the laptop topped out at 108.5 F, toward the back where the CPU lives. Internally, the Core 5 320’s cores averaged a toasty 87.49 degrees Celsius, with the pair of P cores occasionally spiking to 100 C (TJMax), indicating there is some thermal throttling.
The high temps here perhaps explain in part why Dell opted to use two fans in the XPS 13. And while there is some light fan noise when the laptop is under heavy CPU stress, the sound isn’t sharp or otherwise annoying – at least to my middle-aged ears.
Webcam on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
The webcam on the XPS 13 is “only” 1080p, but it delivered enough detail, generally accurate colors, and handled bright light from windows and overhead fixtures pretty well. And unlike some of the XPS models from yesteryear, it also sits in the top center of the bezel, where it belongs.
There is some graininess when viewing things at full screen, but it’s far from the worst I’ve seen. This camera is perfectly capable of handling typical online meetings or classes without making most people want to plug in one of the best webcams instead.
Software on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
Considering its fairly affordable price, I was pleasantly surprised at how clean and pristine the Windows 11 Home OS is on the XPS 13. You get some of the typical Windows cruft, like a shortcut to WhatsApp and LinkedIn. And there are a few Dell apps, like Optimizer (which mostly links to Windows settings and other apps) and the self-explanatory SupportAssistant. But there really isn’t anything else here, other than a bookmark in the default Edge browser to go to McAfee's website. It’s refreshing to use a new laptop with a Windows install that reminds me of custom-built PCs.
Dell XPS 13 (2026) Configurations
Dell offers the XPS 13 in two pretty similar configurations. For $699, you get an Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU with a 512GB SSD and 8GB of RAM. For $200 more ($899), you get the same laptop with 16GB of RAM. Somewhat annoyingly, the 16GB model is only offered in the silver “sky” colorway, while the 8GB model is available in both “sky” and a darker gray “storm.”
Keeping the SKUs simple is doubtlessly one way that Dell is keeping costs down. And obviously the cost and availability of RAM and storage is tough this year. But it still would be nice to see at least a 1TB option for those who need more room for local files.
Bottom Line
While it’s no performance powerhouse, and $200 extra for a doubling of the RAM to a more comfortable 16GB still feels like a lot even in these times of endless AI demand, Dell’s redesigned XPS 13 is an excellent budget or mid-range machine (depending on which model you choose). It’s light and slim enough that you’ll likely hardly notice it in a backpack, and with over 14 hours of battery life in our testing, it lasts longer than the MacBook Neo.
Is it better than the MacBook Neo? In some ways, like the aforementioned battery life, keyboard backlighting, and weight, it is for sure. And for those worried about the limitations of 8GB, you can at least pay extra (again, that’s $200 extra) for 16GB with the XPS system. Really, though, the two devices are close enough in terms of performance, build quality, and portability that, if you are considering one or the other, you should probably choose the one with the operating system you prefer.
The fact that Windows has a competitive machine to the disruptive MacBook Neo is a triumph for Dell, for Microsoft’s ecosystem, and for those of us (like me) who would just prefer not to get sucked into the Apple hardware orbit – not that Windows 11 doesn’t have a big basket full of flaws. Given how expensive everything else is these days (including most flagship premium laptops), it’s nice that Dell and Apple are delivering devices that look and feel good, without costing $1,000 or more. I wonder what the other PC makers will offer up to compete in this new $699-$899 premium laptop space.
After a rough start with the Mattel Aquarius as a child, Matt built his first PC in the late 1990s and ventured into mild PC modding in the early 2000s. He’s spent the last 15 years covering emerging technology for Smithsonian, Popular Science, and Consumer Reports, while testing components and PCs for Computer Shopper, PCMag and Digital Trends.

articles.title: NASA study finds Earth fungi could survive up to 7 days near lunar south pole
articles.text:
In a nutshell: NASA researchers have identified areas near the Moon's south pole where microbes from Earth could survive for days, raising new concerns about contamination as future lunar missions approach. The finding challenges the assumption that the lunar surface is uniformly hostile to terrestrial life, particularly as human exploration increasingly shifts toward the polar region.
The study, published in Science Advances, examined several areas being considered for Artemis landings, including Nobile Rim and Connecting Ridge. Researchers used data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter to model surface conditions, then compared them with the known survival limits of bacteria and fungi commonly found on spacecraft.
Most of the Moon is exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, radiation, and ultraviolet light. However, some polar terrain remains in shadow and receives only indirect light. These locations are also extremely cold, which can help preserve microbes rather than kill them quickly.
The team found that several of these sites could support microbial survival for short periods. In the models, the fungus Aspergillus survived for as long as seven Earth days in some shaded areas.
"Aspergillus was our champion, and possesses characteristics (thick walls and dark pigments that protect them from X-rays, cosmic radiation, and UV-C radiation) that make it especially well suited to survive in regions of the lunar poles," said Prabal Saxena, a research space scientist at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center who led the study, in an email to 404 Media.
The study examined survival, not growth. The microbes would likely become dormant in the lunar environment rather than reproduce or spread. Still, their ability to persist for days means spacecraft could introduce Earth organisms into areas that may be important for scientific research or future exploration.
NASA's Artemis program and a Chinese-Russian space partnership are both pursuing crewed missions to the lunar south pole in the 2030s. The region is a major target because permanently shadowed areas may contain water ice, which could be used for life support and other mission needs.
The same conditions that make these areas promising targets for ice also distinguish them from the rest of the lunar surface. Reduced exposure to sunlight and radiation could allow certain microbes carried aboard spacecraft to remain viable longer than expected.
"Recent studies have shown how unique the conditions are on the surface of the lunar poles and we realized that it was worth studying how amenable those might be to survival for certain microbes, particularly in the context of recent work on how hardy some bacteria and fungi are when exposed to space conditions," Saxena said.
The research combined studies of lunar surface conditions, microbial biology, and planetary protection. Saxena said the team drew on specialists at NASA Goddard in fields including lunar evolution, clean-room microbiology, biochemistry, and lunar lighting.
The potential survival zones were more extensive than researchers had expected.
Saxena said researchers initially expected that a small number of microbes might briefly endure in permanently shadowed areas because those sites receive limited light and radiation while remaining extremely cold. However, the modeling showed that the potential survival zones were broader, and the survival window longer, than the team had anticipated.
The findings may require mission planners to take a closer look at how spacecraft are cleaned and how landing sites are selected. Contamination could affect efforts to study the Moon's history, especially in areas that may preserve material from Earth, the Sun, and space.
The team also noted that microbes could have reached the Moon naturally through debris exchanged between Earth and the Moon.
Saxena said material is regularly exchanged between Earth and the Moon through particles and meteorites, while impacts from elsewhere in the solar system continually strike the lunar surface, making the transfer of microbes possible.
"In many ways, the Moon is a potential time capsule of the Earth, Sun and space environment over time. We should go explore it to see what secrets are waiting to be discovered!"

articles.title: Adobe expands generative AI audio with Firefly music, speech and sound effects - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Adobe expands generative AI audio with Firefly music, speech and sound effects
Adobe Inc. today announced the general availability of audio capabilities in Firefly, the company’s all-in-one creative AI tool suite, allowing users to produce music, speech, and sound effects for their projects.
In June, the company unveiled big changes for Firefly, including a large number of skills for Firefly AI Assistant that built in agentic capabilities for Elements – the company’s user-friendly video and photo editing tool suite – that allowed users to introduce characters, locations and objects that stay the same across projects.
Today’s new tools include generators for music, speech and sound effects.
Generate Music is powered by Firefly Music Model under the hood and creates universally licensed original tracks designed for a user’s own video’s length and mood, so the music can go with whatever content is being generated without worries about copyright issues. It can also be fine-tuned to match the brand and presentation.
Generate Speech uses both Firefly Speech and an option for a model from ElevenLabs Inc. It can take a script and turn it into a fluid, natural voiceover that allows for control over voice, cadence and emotion. ElevenLabs is known for extremely powerful speech models that cover a wide variety of synthetic voices with varied capabilities, emotionality and control.
The sound effect tool also includes an underlying Firefly model that creates custom effects using a prompt, following the timing and energy of the content to produce an appropriate sound.
“Going back to school and trying to stay consistent as a content creator can get really overwhelming,” said Esther Rehema, a fashion, beauty and lifestyle creator. “Being able to find music that is safe for commercial use and fits my content is such a game-changer.”
Adobe added that the audio produced by Firefly Studio is production-quality and commercially safe, like everything else generated by its AI models. No separate subscription is needed for any track generated by the tool.
AI audio generation tools, from music to special effects, have been trending for years. This includes audio tools such as Lyra 3 from Google LLC, OpenAI Group PBC’s reported music-generation experiments and Stability AI Ltd.’s Stable Audio open-source model.

articles.title: Karetic Energy is building iron-air batteries to store power for days rather than hours
articles.text:
Karetic Energy is building iron-air batteries to store power for days rather than hours
The company is developing long-duration storage using iron and air, aimed at the multi-day gaps that solar and wind leave and that lithium cannot economically fill.
A grid running on solar and wind has a timing problem that gets worse as it gets cleaner. Storage covering a few hours handles the evening peak. It does not handle a still, overcast week, and lithium batteries at that duration stop making economic sense long before they stop working.
Iron-air chemistry is one of the answers being tried worldwide. The cell charges and discharges by rusting iron and then reversing the rust. Iron, air and water are abundant and inexpensive materials.
is working on it in India. Founded by Dr Suryanarayana Vikrant Karra and Prabhakar Kumar, the company describes an iron-air battery platform using rare-earth-free, non-flammable aqueous chemistry, aimed at long-duration storage at grid scale.
Two of those words carry commercial weight. Rare-earth-free means the supply chain does not run through the small number of countries that refine those materials. Non-flammable is a safety property the company claims for its chemistry, and safety is what governs where a large battery can be installed.
Rust, reversed
The engineering difficulty in iron-air is not the idea but the side reactions. When you push current through an iron electrode in water, some of the energy goes into splitting the water and producing hydrogen instead of doing the work you wanted, and the iron surface tends to passivate, forming a layer that stops the reaction.
The company says its answer is an iron-particulate bed architecture that suppresses both: hydrogen evolution and surface passivation. On its account, that has delivered continuous discharge cycles of 100 to 145 hours in laboratory conditions, at what it describes as significantly lower capital cost than lithium-ion.
A hundred hours is four days, which is the specific gap the company describes: multi-day flexibility that short-duration storage cannot economically bridge.
The applications it names are utility-scale storage, industrial microgrids and renewable farms, with the systems described as modular and pilot-ready. Its stated positioning is that the platform is ready for utilities to trial rather than still in the laboratory, though the performance figures it quotes are laboratory ones. Those two things are not the same, and the gap between them is what a pilot exists to close.
A million dollars, and nothing in the field
Karetic Energy reports about $0.7 million in funding and a further $0.3 million in grants. It was selected for Bharat Innovates 2026, the government programme that took Indian deep-technology companies to Nice, France, in June, where it presented itself as looking for utility partners and integration opportunities.
What has not been announced is a pilot, a customer, a partner or an independent test result. The company is about eighteen months old, and what exists publicly is a laboratory result and a technical description of how it was achieved. For a storage technology, the distance between that and a utility trial is measured in years.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: ChatGPT peut maintenant écrire et envoyer vos textos
articles.text:
La dernière mise à jour de l’application de bureau ChatGPT pour macOS permet maintenant de se connecter directement avec l’application iMessage d’Apple. Une nouveauté disponible sur les abonnements ChatGPT Work et Codex sur ordinateur.
Quand ChatGPT prend le contrôle de vos messages
Ce nouveau plugin prend en charge les échanges sous iMessage, les SMS traditionnels et le protocole RCS sur macOS. Depuis la fenêtre de ChatGPT, l’IA est en mesure de balayer votre historique pour retrouver une donnée précise, de rédiger des brouillons ou d’envoyer directement un message à un contact. Dans le cadre d’une présentation commerciale, vous aurez par exemple la possibilité d’analyser les textes de votre rendez-vous pour suggérer automatiquement des relances pertinentes. Vous pourrez aussi demander de nettoyer votre boîte de réception en supprimant les spams par commande vocale. OpenAI précise que cette extension demande un Mac équipé d’une puce Apple Silicon et ne fonctionne donc pas sur les anciennes machines équipées de processeurs Intel.
 Everyday conversations just got easier with the new Apple Messages plugin.
Search messages, catch up on conversations, draft and send replies—all with ChatGPT on your Mac.
Now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex on desktop. pic.twitter.com/nicfZMuxZc
— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) August 20, 2026
Vient maintenant la question épineuse de la confidentialité et de la sécurité des données. L’entreprise veut évidemment vous rassurer en affirmant que le module tourne localement sur votre machine et n’envoie pas vos discussions sur les serveurs. L’envoi de textos reste aussi soumis par défaut à une validation manuelle de votre part concernant le contenu et le destinataire. Vous pouvez évidemment choisir d’approuver la validation automatique par ChatGPT, mais l’entreprise elle-même met en garde contre l’activation de cette option qui supprime la dernière vérification humaine avant l’expédition d’un message en votre nom. Pas si rassurant que ça, finalement.
De nouvelles options pour le travail d’équipe
Les fonctionnalités liées à la messagerie ne sont pas les seules nouveautés annoncées par OpenAI, qui en profite également pour apporter des améliorations autour de l’organisation et de la collaboration. Les discussions épinglées sont par exemple enfin synchronisées entre la version ordinateur sur Mac et l’application sur iPhone. ChatGPT autorise aussi maintenant la génération d’images en lecture seule pour partager le résultat d’une session de travail locale depuis Codex ou ChatGPT Work. Les liens créés publiquement restent consultables par quiconque détient l’adresse web, mais la portée des espaces de travail d’entreprise reste limitée à leurs membres.
 Be a homie and don’t gatekeep your best chats 👀
You can now share read-only conversations from both ChatGPT Work and Codex on desktop.
It’s an easy way to show your process or give someone the context behind your work. pic.twitter.com/k9n1YHsGA7
— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) August 20, 2026
Si vous avez un site web hébergé par la plateforme, vous pouvez inviter des coéditeurs qui ont leur propre espace de travail afin de modifier du contenu, actualiser une base de données ou publier des mises à jour. Les créateurs d’origine conservent évidemment le contrôle des accès, du paramétrage et de la restauration des versions. Enfin, l’option « Historique de l’ordinateur », introduite la semaine dernière, commence son déploiement auprès des comptes Pro, Business et Enterprise en Europe, au Royaume-Uni et en Suisse.
 Add teammates as editors to your ChatGPT Sites so you can build and publish together.
Collaborators can push changes to the same project while Codex handles git management and CI behind the scenes. pic.twitter.com/NiG1NQE59i
— OpenAI Developers (@OpenAIDevs) August 20, 2026

articles.title: Bilbao se ha marcado un Alemania: prohibido pagar con Bizum o tarjeta en Aste Nagusia
articles.text:
Sacar el móvil y pagar con él es algo casi tan común como ir a comprar el pan. O con el smartwatch, incluso, olvidándote de cualquier tarjeta física o pasarela intermedia. Sin embargo, algunos lugares todavía se resisten. Bilbao decidió, para su fiesta grande, girar el reloj sin prisa hacia atrás. En plena era del contactless, la Aste Nagusia impuso un único método de cobro en sus txosnas: billetes y monedas. Ni Bizum, ni tarjeta, ni QR de banco. Metálico al canto.
La medida llega de Bilboko Konpartsak, la federación que agrupa a 27 comparsas y monta cada agosto las txosnas (o casetas) del recinto ferial del Arenal. Y Bizum, tarjeta o PayPal se quedan fuera, métodos que llegaron mucho después de 1978, el año en que nació el actual modelo participativo de la fiesta.
Por qué evitar el digital. El portavoz Iker Martín resumió los motivos: las comisiones bancarias restan dinero a un movimiento popular y voluntario que no persigue beneficio; la cobertura móvil falla en horas punta y arriesga dejar una caja sin cerrar a las dos de la madrugada. Además, digitalizar cada ticket encaja mal con una organización que ya sustituyó los vasos de plástico por reutilizables en nombre del ecologismo.
2026 ha sido el año clave, porque ha sido cuando ha entrado en juego Batuz, el sistema de control de facturación que exige TicketBAI a cualquier entidad que factura más de 50.000 euros en nueve días (además del LROE, el libro contable de ingresos y gastos). La Norma Foral 4/2019 convierte a estas casetas bilbainas en las únicas de toda Bizkaia obligadas a control fiscal, pese a tratarse de agrupaciones sin ánimo de lucro. ¿La paradoja? Factura electrónica sí, pago electrónico no (el TPV emite el ticket en papel; el dinero, mientras, sigue circulando en mano. Y ante reclamaciones, Bilboko Konpartsak recomienda ticket digital.
La fiesta más importante. Marijaia y Gargantúa (los emblemáticos personales que velan por esta Semana Grande) llevan saliendo a la calle durante 46 ediciones. 37 txosnas autorizadas en El Arenal. La fiesta empieza mañana, 22 de agosto, y termina el 30 de agosto. Y quieren recuperar la participación de antaño, con un programa que va desde manifiestos, mediometrajes, eventos deportivos, sesiones de DJ con Óscar Martínez y muchos conciertos, como los de Bebe, M-Clan o Leire, o incluso programas de música clásica, como el de la virtuosa al violín Tatiana Samouil.
2025 convocó a 1,5 millones de personas repartidas entre más de 500 actividades gratuitas (por debajo del millón seiscientas mil de 2024 y lejos del récord de 1,8 millones marcado en 2022). Los fuegos artificiales sumaron 900.000 espectadores; el Txikigune infantil, 90.000; los más de cien conciertos gratuitos, 200.000. La policía practicó 165 detenciones, siete más que el año anterior. Aunque si hay algo que estropea las fiestas es una mala lluvia. Al menos la AEMET promete finde soleado.
Dinero contante y sonante. Mientras neobancos como Revolut arrasan, los alemanes se resisten. El Bundesbank cifró en 51% la proporción de pagos en efectivo en 2023, todavía mayoritaria pese a la caída desde el 58% de 2021 y el 83% de 2008. Cada alemán lleva de media 107 euros en la cartera, según el propio banco central. ¿La explicación? La privacidad. El Oktoberfest de Múnich funcionó dos siglos solo con metálico: aunque ya aceptan tarjeta, siguen prefiriendo billetes. El guardarropa del mítico Berghain, templo del tecno berlinés, solo cobra en efectivo.
Otras regiones de Europa también se resisten, como el sur de Italia (Nápoles o Salerno), o el de Polonia (Cracovia, toda la subcarpacia). Las sagre italianas, fiestas de pueblo que organizan asociaciones vecinales sin ánimo de lucro, rondan las 20.000 ediciones al año y muchas siguen sin datáfono. En los matsuri japoneses, los puestos de comida callejera (los yatai) ni te molestes en enseñarles algo que no sean monedas de cien yenes. La trazabilidad digital ni ha llegado ni se la espera.

articles.title: No necesitas saber programar: esta app de Meta te permite crear tu propio videojuego con IA
articles.text:
Meta amplió a todos los usuarios de Estados Unidos el acceso a Pocket, su aplicación experimental que permite crear pequeños videojuegos y experiencias interactivas utilizando instrucciones escritas en lenguaje natural.
La herramienta emplea inteligencia artificial para generar los juegos a partir de las indicaciones del usuario, por lo que no es necesario tener conocimientos de programación para comenzar a crear.
PUBLICIDAD
Pocket había sido lanzada discretamente el mes pasado en Brasil como mercado de prueba y ahora llega a un público más amplio en Estados Unidos. Las creaciones aparecen posteriormente en un feed desplazable, donde otros usuarios pueden probarlas, guardarlas, modificarlas para crear nuevas versiones o republicarlas.
La propuesta forma parte de la estrategia de Meta para utilizar la inteligencia artificial no solo como una herramienta para responder preguntas, sino también como un mecanismo para facilitar la creación de contenido y aplicaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Así funciona Pocket para crear videojuegos con IA
El funcionamiento de Pocket parte de una idea sencilla: el usuario describe qué quiere crear mediante una instrucción y la inteligencia artificial genera una experiencia interactiva.
Estos contenidos, que Meta denomina “dispositivos”, pueden responder a diferentes acciones realizadas con el teléfono. Por ejemplo, pueden reaccionar al tacto o a la inclinación del dispositivo, reproducir efectos de sonido e incluso incorporar fragmentos de canciones.
PUBLICIDAD
La aplicación también puede utilizar elementos del propio teléfono. Algunas experiencias permiten utilizar fotografías almacenadas en la galería o acceder a la cámara para incorporarlas a las creaciones.
De esta manera, Pocket busca reducir considerablemente la barrera de entrada que tradicionalmente supone desarrollar un videojuego. En lugar de escribir manualmente cada línea de código, el usuario puede explicar a la inteligencia artificial qué experiencia quiere obtener y dejar que el sistema se encargue de generar la parte técnica.
PUBLICIDAD
Los juegos se pueden compartir y modificar
Una vez creada una experiencia, esta puede publicarse en el perfil del usuario dentro de Pocket. Otros miembros de la comunidad pueden interactuar con ella y, además, tienen la posibilidad de guardarla, republicarla o remezclarla para desarrollar una nueva creación.
Este componente social es una parte importante de la propuesta. Meta no busca únicamente ofrecer una herramienta para crear juegos individuales, sino construir un catálogo de experiencias generadas por los propios usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
El sistema de recomendaciones puede ayudar a distribuir esas creaciones dentro del feed, permitiendo que determinados juegos alcancen una mayor audiencia.
Pocket nació tras una adquisición de Meta
El desarrollo de Pocket está relacionado con la adquisición que Meta realizó a principios de este año del equipo detrás de Gizmo, una plataforma especializada en experiencias interactivas creadas mediante código.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía ha utilizado parte de esa tecnología para desarrollar el concepto de “codificación de ambiente”, que busca facilitar la creación de software mediante instrucciones en lenguaje natural en lugar de exigir que el usuario escriba código tradicionalmente.
Pocket representa así una aplicación práctica de esa estrategia: transformar una idea expresada con palabras en una experiencia que puede ejecutarse e interactuar con ella desde el teléfono.
PUBLICIDAD
Meta quiere acelerar la creación de nuevas aplicaciones
La llegada de Pocket también se enmarca en una estrategia más amplia de Meta para desarrollar aplicaciones independientes y experimentar con nuevos formatos.
La compañía ya ha lanzado otras propuestas como Instagram Instants, Forum, una aplicación independiente relacionada con Grupos, y Seller, orientada a las funciones de Marketplace.
PUBLICIDAD
Meta también ha experimentado con herramientas de creación de imágenes y vídeos mediante inteligencia artificial. A esto se suma una aplicación experimental centrada en la creación de vídeos y, más recientemente, la llegada de Meta AI a Mac.
Mark Zuckerberg explicó durante la presentación de resultados de la compañía en julio que el desarrollo de software con inteligencia artificial permite a Meta probar y lanzar nuevas ideas con mayor rapidez.
La estrategia consiste en experimentar con diferentes productos y utilizar los sistemas de recomendación de la compañía para determinar cuáles tienen potencial para crecer.
Con Pocket, Meta lleva esta filosofía al terreno de los videojuegos: una persona sin conocimientos de programación puede pasar de tener una idea a crear una pequeña experiencia interactiva utilizando únicamente instrucciones para la inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: GitHub now sees 2.9 billion commits a month -- and it can't keep up
articles.text:
GitHub now sees 2.9 billion commits a month — and it can’t keep up
Per month, GitHub now sees 2.9 billion commits, 130 million merged pull requests, and 24 million new repos. Back in April, GitHub already had a hard time handling ‘only’ 1.4 billion commits.
To a large degree, that’s thanks to how popular coding agents have become and how quickly software development is changing. But it’s also no secret that GitHub, despite its efforts to move to a more modern architecture, simply hasn’t been able to scale fast enough to meet this demand.
“We have made progress, but these incidents make clear that we must accelerate this work.” — GitHub CTO Vlad Fedorov.
Why GitHub went down on August 17
The new data comes from a postmortem of its August 17 outage, which lasted almost eight hours. That was GitHub’s second major outage in August alone.
As GitHub CTO Vlad Fedorov notes in the postmortem, “We have made progress, but these incidents make clear that we must accelerate this work.”
He stresses that the outage was due to scaling issues, not any code changes. GitHub’s infrastructure ran out of capacity, and those issues cascaded into this outage.
“Our investigation found that the outage began when traffic reached a new peak, and a critical infrastructure component in our Central US data center failed to scale with it,” he explains. “The resulting capacity pressure spread through our systems, causing authentication failures and disrupting multiple GitHub services.”
3M new CPU cores and GitHub still can’t keep up
It’s worth noting that this is not because GitHub isn’t scaling its infrastructure. Fedorov used the post to disclose that 58% of GitHub’s platform load is now served by Azure. That’s up from 12% in May. Half of all Git operations are now served by Azure, too.
The team added 3 million CPU cores this year, as well as 120 petabytes of high-speed storage, Fedorov writes.
As for GitHub’s own data center, that’s maxed out now. “We installed as much hardware as available power allowed in our existing data centers while accelerating our migration to Azure,” Fedorov says.
He also acknowledges that GitHub is facing other challenges as well.
“As the pace and complexity of change increased, our existing operational practices did not keep up. We have redirected teams and resources toward availability and invested in stronger testing, safer rollouts, better observability, and more effective alerting. We have made progress, but this work is not complete,” he writes. “In addition, we are also isolating critical systems and removing shared dependencies between them. This work is designed to reduce the likelihood of an outage and limit its impact when one occurs.”
For now, to avoid the issues that triggered the recent outages, GitHub is making a few concrete changes: it’s applying consistent retry limits and budgets, and tweaking timeouts across service-to-service interactions “to prevent retry storms and cascading load,” as Fedorov writes.
A creaking GitHub is an opportunity for others
GitHub is central to the developer ecosystem — and especially the open source ecosystem. Its recent issues, however, have created an opening for others to launch competing products.
That includes Entire, the startup founded by GitHub’s former CEO Thomas Dohmke, which is betting on a distributed system to better handle agent-driven development workloads. With Origin, Cursor, too, is getting into this game.

articles.title: Modern Warfare 4 beta includes a campaign mission, Switch 2 support, and background shader compilation
articles.text:
Highly anticipated: This year's pre-release Call of Duty beta will include several features never before included in a beta, allowing interested parties to test most of the final game's modes. Players will also catch their first glimpse of the Nintendo Switch 2 version, and a new PC feature aims to reduce the time spent waiting for shaders to compile.
Activision has revealed the start date, contents, and system requirements for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's open beta. Like prior betas, it mostly centers on multiplayer content but will also include a campaign mission for the first time.
A brief trailer reveals that the mission, titled "Entrenched," includes snowy trench warfare, with players controlling a South Korean soldier amid a modern-day North Korean invasion. The initial reveal trailer showcased additional globetrotting missions starring franchise hero Captain Price.
Meanwhile, the first phase of the beta, available to customers who pre-order, also includes six multiplayer maps and eight modes: Team Deathmatch, Domination, Hardpoint, Kill Confirmed, Inflation, Search & Destroy, Kill Block, and Mobility Course. The early access beta will be available from 2 PM ET on August 21 to 1 PM on August 25 on Steam, Battle.net, the Microsoft Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. Pre-loads begin at noon on August 20.
The following week, the open beta, available to all players, runs from 1 PM on August 28 to 1 PM on September 1. It adds two Ground War maps, a Warzone map, two multiplayer maps, and support for Nintendo Switch 2. Pre-orders for Switch 2 will also open when beta pre-loads begin at noon on August 26.
Despite ending support for last-generation consoles and introducing new ray tracing features, Modern Warfare 4's beta system requirements mirror the final specs for last year's entry, Black Ops 7. Activision claims that the beta is playable on aging graphics cards such as the AMD Radeon RX 470 and Nvidia GeForce GTX 970 with as little as 3GB of VRAM. Even the recommended specs only demand an RX 6700 XT or RTX 3060 Ti with 8GB of VRAM. As was the case last year, TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot are also required.
To minimize time spent waiting after the first boot-up, the beta can compile shaders without the game being launched. After installing or updating the beta, PC users will receive a Windows system tray notification announcing that pre-compiling has started while displaying a progress percentage. Steam users must also briefly compile additional shaders after boot-up, but Battle.net performs the entire process in the background. Activision claims that shader pre-compilation consumes minimal system resources, freeing players to use their PCs while waiting.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Battle.net, Steam, and Nintendo Switch 2 on October 23.

iPhone 16 registra queda superior a 40% em oferta na Amazon
iPhone 16 (128 GB) traz tela OLED de 2.000 nits e câmera principal de 48 MP; celular da Apple sai 41% mais barato do que preço original no Pix
O iPhone 16 de 128 GB está saindo por R$ 4.599 no Pix na Amazon. O celular da Apple lançado em 2024 com câmera principal de 48 MP e tela OLED de até 2.000 nits recebe nesta oferta desconto de 41% sobre o preço original de R$ 7.799.
O iPhone 16 é equipado com uma tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″, que possui taxa de 60 Hz e brilho de até 2.000 nits, combinação capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores realistas, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield garante proteção ao display em acidentes diversos.
Seu chip Apple A18 e os 8 GB de RAM permitem rodar apps pesados em multitarefa e executar soluções da suíte Apple Intelligence. Embora 128 GB de armazenamento seja pouco para a maioria, dá para ser expandido com planos do iCloud.

articles.title: YouTube Premium augmente ses prix en Europe : la France est-elle concernée ?
articles.text:
C’est a priori une mauvaise nouvelle pour les abonnés de YouTube Premium en Europe. Depuis le 20 août 2026, plusieurs signalements circulent sur Reddit : des utilisateurs disent avoir été avertis d’une nouvelle hausse de prix, notamment au Portugal et en Italie. D’autres témoignages font également état d’une augmentation dans plusieurs pays européens, comme la Finlande.
Le média The Next Web a quant à lui pu consulter la notification reçue par un abonné roumain : le tarif de son forfait individuel passe de 29 à 32 lei par mois, soit une augmentation d’environ 10 %. Une hausse qui doit permettre à YouTube de « continuer à améliorer Premium et de soutenir les créateurs et les artistes que vous suivez », selon le message consulté par le média.
Google n’a pour l’instant pas annoncé publiquement de nouvelle hausse généralisée à l’ensemble de l’Europe. Mais les notifications envoyées aux abonnés commencent à confirmer qu’une nouvelle vague d’augmentations est en cours dans plusieurs pays.
YouTube Premium n’a pas le même prix partout
Cette nouvelle hausse rappelle surtout une particularité de YouTube Premium : Google ne pratique pas un tarif unique à l’échelle mondiale, ni même en Europe. Le prix dépend du pays de souscription, des taxes locales, mais aussi parfois du canal utilisé pour s’abonner.
Au Portugal, plusieurs utilisateurs de Reddit disent par exemple avoir reçu une notification annonçant une hausse de leur abonnement de 17,99 à 20,99 euros par mois. En Finlande, d’autres évoquent un passage de 14,99 à 16,99 euros. Ces montants reposant, pour l’instant, sur des témoignages d’abonnés.
En France, l’abonnement individuel à YouTube Premium coûte actuellement 12,99 euros par mois sur le Web. La formule étudiante est proposée à 7,99 euros, tandis que l’abonnement familial atteint 29,99 euros par mois.
La dernière hausse française connue a justement concerné ce dernier. En juillet 2025, Google avait fait passer le forfait famille de 23,99 à 29,99 euros par mois, soit six euros de plus. Le prix de la formule individuelle, lui, n’a pas bougé depuis août 2023, lorsqu’il était passé de 11,99 à 12,99 euros.
Il faut noter que ces montants peuvent être différents sur iPhone et iPad. L’App Store français affiche actuellement l’abonnement individuel à 16,99 euros par mois, contre 12,99 euros en passant directement par YouTube sur le Web. Premium Lite y coûte également 9,99 euros, contre 7,99 euros sur le Web. Les tarifs proposés via l’App Store sont donc plus élevés.
Google multiplie désormais les formules pour YouTube
Une éventuelle hausse française interviendrait alors que Google a largement diversifié ses offres autour de YouTube Premium. Premium Lite est disponible en France depuis juillet 2025 pour 7,99 euros par mois.
Depuis mars 2026, la formule permet aussi la lecture en arrière-plan et le téléchargement de la plupart des vidéos, tout en conservant certaines limitations : des publicités restent présentes sur les contenus musicaux, les Shorts ou encore certaines pages, et YouTube Music Premium n’est pas inclus.
Google a également commencé à intégrer des avantages YouTube à certains abonnements Gemini (l’IA de Google). Selon le pays, Google AI Pro peut inclure YouTube Premium Lite, tandis que Google AI Ultra peut inclure l’offre individuelle complète de YouTube Premium.
Pour l’instant, rien ne confirme qu’une nouvelle hausse soit en cours en France, mais ça sent tout de même le sapin. En cas d’augmentation, Google prévient ses abonnés au moins 30 jours à l’avance et, dans certaines régions, leur demande d’accepter explicitement le nouveau tarif pour conserver leur abonnement.

articles.title: Sennheiser Unveils the Momentum True Wireless 5 Earbuds with User Replaceable Batteries
articles.text:
Thursday, August 20th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Sennheiser Unveils the Momentum True Wireless 5 Earbuds with User Replaceable Batteries
The Sennheiser brand today announces Momentum True Wireless 5, its most advanced true wireless earbuds yet, engineered for an uncompromising listening experience wherever life takes you. Reimagined from the inside-out, they combine intelligent innovation with the inspired engineering of their full-size Momentum 5 Wireless counterpart, bringing flagship performance into a beautifully compact design.
Frank Foppe, Product Manager"We set out to bring the larger-than-life sound and connected technology of the Momentum series into a remarkably compact format," "From its exquisite audio reproduction to the advanced hardware powering it all, Momentum True Wireless 5 represents our most advanced integration of audio technology in an earbud."
Key Highlights:
The heart of the earbuds is the same sound-first DNA that powers the recently released fifth-gen Momentum headphones, letting listeners choose their preferred wearing style for listening without compromise. It all starts with the brand's signature 7 mm TrueResponse dynamic transducer, capable of balancing remarkable detail with full-bodied, bass-driven tuning. Meticulously developed at the brand's production facility in Tullamore, Ireland, each transducer is manufactured and tested for exceptional precision, clarity and dynamics. Bluetooth 6.0 with aptX Adaptive codec support provides stable wireless freedom for a crystal-clear hi-res audio pathway up to 24-bit and 96 kHz, including aptX Lossless for bit-perfect transmission on supported audio sources.
The bar for acoustic performance is raised once again, highlighted by the revised adaptive hybrid active noise cancellation (ANC) system and automatic anti-wind mode. A redesigned ear tip works in tandem with a dedicated four-microphone array to maximize noise cancelling performance while delivering the series' most natural-sounding, real-time transparency mode to date. For pristine voice capture, the earbuds engage all eight system sensors—combining six microphones and two bone-conduction voice accelerometers with an AI speech-extraction algorithm to isolate the voice in chaotic environments.
Inheriting the spatial audio prowess of the over-ear model, Momentum True Wireless 5 is fully optimized for Dolby Atmos with interactive head-tracking capability, projecting an immersive, theater-like spatial audio field that you can take anywhere.
Eco-Conscious Endurance
Momentum True Wireless 5 is built to last, introducing a user-replaceable battery system in both the earbuds and wireless charging case, letting users easily refresh the power cells in mere minutes. Sharing the same ethos as the brand's flagship Momentum 5 headphones, customers can safeguard their technology and retain the earbuds' longevity far beyond standard battery degradation using only a compact screwdriver.
Designed for all-day listening, the earbuds further improve their endurance over the prior generation with 12 hours of continuous playback per charge, and over two additional replenishments stored in the Qi-enabled wireless charging case for up to 40 total hours of run time. The quick charge capability extends listening up to 1 hour from just an 8-minute top-up.
Lilika Beck, President of Sennheiser Consumer Hearing"Balancing compact size, our signature high-fidelity acoustics, and a replaceable battery is a major breakthrough," "With Momentum True Wireless 5, we are proving that cutting-edge performance does not have to sacrifice longevity."
Ergonomic Evolution 
To achieve their "barely there" fit, the earbud housing features an elegant new aerodynamic silhouette sculpted using data derived from thousands of unique ear models. The earbuds' fin-less shape was rated more comfortable than the prior generation by 73% of testers, and is rated IP54 for dust, sweat and splash resistance, A micro-perforated acoustic mic plate mitigates wind turbulence, protecting both voice capture and ANC stability from aerodynamic interference. The companion charging case has also been re-engineered with a narrower, pocket-friendly aspect ratio and a low-friction finish for seamless ingress and egress from tight pockets.
Ready for the Future Today
Momentum True Wireless 5 is a connectivity king, bringing a frictionless experience to a wide range of audio sources:
Momentum True Wireless 5 will be available in five luxurious metallic colorways: Graphite, Cream, Graphite, Copper, Denim, and Lavender. The earbuds will begin shipping on September 3rd from sennheiser-hearing.com and select retailers at an MSRP of $299.95 USD.
